item.title: Sauk Rapids' winningest senior class 'playing for themselves' after quarterfinal loss
item.description: ST. PAUL, Minn. — When the six Sauk Rapids-Rice volleyball seniors were freshmen, Storm volleyball had not been what it is today: a back-to-back 20-win Section 8AAA champion for the first time in school history while boasting four consecutive winning seasons. More: St. Cloud-area runners shine at 2026 MSHSL State Championships More: Sauk Rapids volleyball sweeps Little Falls, 'knows what it takes' for state run On Nov. 11, the graduating class took the court with a fighting chance to win a state championship for the final time against Princeton, losing 3-0 (25-20, 25-16, 25-21). The seniors — setter Emma Sunby, defensive specialist Elliyana Karl, right side Peyton Welch, libero Abbey Meinert, middle Molly Warzecha and outside hitter Josie Anderson — saw four consecutive losing seasons from 2019-22 before joining the team freshman year. "It's a very special group," head coach Gail Bialke said. "It's amazing what we've done in the last four years at Sauk Rapids with these girls as our leaders. We had a really strong class last year, and to come back to [state] is just unremarkable." It's the first time in school history that the Storm made it to consecutive state tournaments for volleyball and will be making room in the high school gym for a new banner after running out of space on its current one hanging. Highlighted by a fifth-place finish at state to cap off a 27-3 campaign in 2025, the '26 senior class accumulated an 81-28 record across their four seasons, the winningest class in at least the last 20 years. The friendship off the court is what keeps the wins coming. "These are genuinely my best friends," Meinert said. "I've known them since seventh grade when volleyball started, and it's cool to see each other grow. These two [Josie and Emma] are just such wonderful women. It's a memory that I will remember for the rest of my life, and I'm just so grateful to be here playing next to my best friends." In front of a full student section bussed down to the arena, the Storm got out to a strong start in their state championship quest with an 8-4 lead in the first set but failed to see a lead for the rest of the night. Princeton's strong hitting and inept ability to extend rallies became too much for the Storm, falling quickly behind in the second set as the Tigers scored at will on their way to a second-set triumph. item.title: Pedro Porro talks Barcelona interest, Lamine Yamal and Pau Cubarsi
item.description: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - JULY 14: Pedro Porro of Spain celebrates his goal with Lamine Yamal of Spain during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Semi Final match between France and Spain at Dallas Stadium on July 14, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Image Photo Agency/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pedro Porro has been linked with a move to Barcelona this season and has opened up on the transfer talk, as well as Barcelona stars Lamine Yamal and Pau Cubarsí, while on international duty with Spain. The Tottenham defender says he’s flattered by reported interest from the Catalan giants and talk that Joan Laporta sees him as the “dream” defensive signing for Barca. “Yes, of course it is a compliment. When one of the best clubs in the world is interested in you, or at least that’s what they say, it’s always good, because I’m surely doing my job well. We must continue in the same vein,” he told Sport. “It is also a compliment on [Laporta’s] part. As I said before, it is good that, for example, the president of another club that is not mine values the work. It surely means that I am doing things right.” Porro also spoke about playing alongside Lamine Yamal for the national team and the connection he has with the Barcelona teenager. “Very good. The truth is that in this World Cup I also gained more confidence with him,” he added. “As I have always said, he is a wonderful boy, who helps you and contributes a lot to the team. For me it’s a privilege to play with him because he’s the best.” Cubarsi is another Barcelona teenager playing with Porro for Spain, and the Tottenham defender thinks he will become one of the best center-backs in the world.. “Yes, for me it’s amazing. I see him up close in the national team and he is an extraordinary player,” he said. “As you say, at 19 years old he has already achieved a lot of things, but I also say that because of the player he is. To have that mentality being so young… I think he’s going to be one of the best centre-backs in the world.” Cubarsi has joined up with Spain after being crowned the winner of the Golden Boy Award for 2026 , following a year that brought La Liga success with Barcelona and a World Cup with La Roja.

item.title: Astros GM Randy Flores: Hiring Brad Ausmus as manager was 'choice I wanted to make'
item.description: The hiring of Brad Ausmus as Astros manager fuels questions about Randy Flores' decision-making power. Houston's new GM details insisted the former catcher with longtime ties to the franchise was his choice. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) LAS VEGAS - Before arriving at the general managers' meetings, Randy Flores flew to the San Diego area on Saturday to meet with Brad Ausmus . The two spent half the day together, Flores said, after which the Houston Astros general manager came away "very confident" he had found his new manager. The Astros named Ausmus their next manager Wednesday , handing the role to the former catcher who spent 10 seasons of his 18-year playing career in Houston. Wednesday afternoon at the Aria, Flores detailed the process that led him - and the Astros - to that decision. Ausmus' hire likely fueled questions about influence within Houston's front office and Flores' decision-making power as its new GM. Ausmus has a strong relationship from his playing days with Jeff Bagwell, the former first baseman and now Astros senior advisor who is a trusted voice to owner Jim Crane, and reportedly interviewed for the team's GM vacancy last month prior to Flores being hired. Crane said Flores would "take over" the managerial search upon arrival but that the Astros had already interviewed "a few" candidates. Ausmus being one of those invited questions about how the hiring process unfolded. Flores described it from his perspective Wednesday, saying that Ausmus was "the choice I wanted to make" for manager. Flores said he interviewed multiple times with Crane for the GM role. In their first interview, Flores said he presented "several" possible candidates for manager, including Ausmus. Flores said that before proposing Ausmus' name he had already talked with people "who he worked under or he was the boss of or he played with, just getting a sense of him." "People that I really trust in this game, people that I've leaned on for 11 years in the game, were like, ‘(He) absolutely deserves an opportunity,'" Flores said. "That's what I heard over and over." In their second interview, Flores said, Crane told him he thought Ausmus would be a "solid candidate." Flores said he later heard the Astros had already talked with Ausmus about the GM opening, but after landing the GM job, Flores still wanted to set up an in-person meeting as he interviewed candidates for the managerial opening. Flores confirmed that he identified four finalists for manager, including Albert Pujols. Morgan Ensberg and Luis Urueta were the other candidates reported to have interviewed. "What I can say is that Jim told me, ‘It's your decision,'" Flores said. He said Crane asked if he wanted to talk to other candidates after the GM meetings but Flores wanted to meet with Ausmus first. item.title: Rutgers WR KJ Duff to Miss Rest of Season After Surgery
item.description: Kj Duff of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights reacts during an NCAA FBS football game at SHI Stadium in Piscataway, United States, on October 3, 2026. (Photo by Dan Squicciarini/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Rutgers football will be without another one of its star talents on offense for the rest of the season, as wide receiver KJ Duff will miss the remainder of the season due to surgery he had earlier this week that is intended to repair a high-ankle injury he sustained during the season. This news comes roughly a week after Kwabena Asamoah was ruled out for the season due to a similar surgery. With this news, the Rutgers star will finish his junior season with 45 catches for 774 yards and nine touchdowns. Two weeks ago, when Rutgers was set to play Michigan, Duff appeared on the injury report as doubtful to play due to an issue with his ankle; however, after working hard to rehab his injury throughout the week, according to Rutgers Head Coach Greg Schiano, he was upgraded to questionable later in the week. He ultimately suited up to play that Saturday. Earlier in that game, after getting rolled up on a few times, Duff went down with an injury and left the field for the remainder of the game. He did not suit up against Wisconsin the next week before it was announced that his season was over. According to multiple reports, Duff should be cleared to resume football activities in January, which will give him time to prepare for the draft. Duff was expected to be a first round draft pick coming into the season, however, it is unknown how much this injury will affect his draft stock. If he does decide to declare for the draft, Duff will finish his career at Rutgers with 132 receptions for 2,283 yards and 17 touchdowns, which will make him top 10 all time in Rutgers history in all three categories.

item.title: 'There were a lot of positives': Freshman Wilson shines in Holy Cross loss
item.description: WORCESTER – As Holy Cross coach Dave Paulsen expected, the start of the 2026-27 season has been challenging as the Crusaders work through inexperience and injuries. HC lost its first two games, to the University of Rhode Island and Villanova, by an average of 36.5 points. Furman, which has emerged as a mid-major power over the last decade, rolled into the Hart Center Nov. 11 to give HC another early test in its home opener. The Crusaders ran with the Paladins and hung in with them into the second half. HC never led but was as close as four points with 10 minutes to play before Furman pulled away for an 80-67 win. “There were a lot of positives,” Paulsen said. “That’s a really good team. I thought we played really, really hard and had some good performances. There were a lot of positives, but on the other hand, we should win that game.” Paulsen thought missed layups, getting hurt on the glass, and HC’s missed free throws (nine of them) were the difference. Holy Cross freshman Tristen Wilson, who was the Patriot League Rookie of the Week after averaging 13 points on 58% shooting in HC’s first two games, was excited for his Hart Center debut and it showed. Wilson posted a double-double with 20 points and 14 rebounds. He added 5 assists and 3 blocks. “Our mentality was to protect the house,” Wilson said. “Let’s getting us going and start building some momentum. We’re starting to get better.” Junior Arius Alijosius, a transfer from Division 2 Lewis in Illinois, scored 17 points and was 5-9 from 3-point territory. Holy Cross and Furman met for just the second time. The Crusaders won the only other game between the schools, 104-88, on Dec. 30, 1971. Furman, which improved to 4-0, averaged 99.3 points in its first three games. The Paladins have won 20 or more games eight times in the last 10 years and reached the NCAA Tournament twice (2023, 2026) in the last four seasons. Furman led by as many as 18 in the first half and was up, 42-28, at halftime. Early in the second, juniors Kole Hanson and Alijosius combined to sink three straight 3s -- Wilson assisted on two of them -- and HC cut the Furman lead to eight. The Paladins built the lead back to double digits, but the Crusaders kept coming. Alijosius buried a 3 off a Hanson steal, Wilson swished a 3 and Alijosius made another one from the corner. An Alijosius steal led to a Wilson layup that had HC within 58-54 with 10:28 left. “Seeing the ball go through the rim helps,” Alijosius said, “but it has to start defensively. item.description: LAS VEGAS – Triston Casas will play for Tigres del Licey of the Dominican Winter League this offseason. The 26-year-old first baseman also played for Licey during the 2022-23 offseason. “I don’t have a definitive date,” said president of baseball operations Craig Breslow. “Still needs to ramp up in terms of game speed and intensity. But he is feeling good, so we’re optimistic he’s gonna be able to compete in Winter League games.” Casas has not played in a major league game since rupturing his left patellar tendon more than 18 months ago on May 2, 2025. He dealt with a left-side intercostal strain earlier in the 2026 season, then underwent arthroscopic wrist surgery in August. “He’s obviously missed a significant amount of time over the last couple of years so we don’t have real workload concerns in terms of total volume,” Breslow said. “We just want to make sure that his body is ready to do what will be asked of it and what’s required of playing in a pretty competitive environment.” Whitlock’s leg injury was a stress fracture As previously reported, imaging revealed that setup man Garrett Whitlock pitched through a fractured tibia late in the 2026 season. Breslow gave the exact diagnosis of “stress fracture” on Wednesday. “My understanding is stress fracture, and so far it’s making good progress,” Breslow said. “I don’t anticipate this to be something that has longer term implications.” Whitlock finished ninth for 2026 AL Reliever of the Year, receiving one second-place vote and two fifth-place votes. He posted a 1.72 ERA, 0.90 WHIP and .204 opponent batting average in 54 games (52 ⅓ innings). item.description: The University of Maryland Men’s Soccer team ended in a tie game against UCLA at Ludwig Field on September 25th 2026. | Jessie Reider/Testudo Times Having kept No. 1-seed Indiana scoreless through the first half of its Big Ten Tournament semifinal game, No. 5-seed Maryland men’s soccer entered the second half with an opportunity to redeem its early-season loss. Unfortunately for the Terps, their resolve dissolved 90 seconds after the break. A corner kick swung in by the Hoosiers wasn’t cleared by Farouk Cisse, with the ball bouncing off his body and back towards the mass of players. Indiana striker Easton Bogard separated from the pack and swung his left foot at the shot; it bounced off the body of Maryland’s Maxwell Sekyi and into the roof of the net. The scrappy 47th-minute goal gave Indiana the victory in a scrappy game, as the Terps fell 1-0 on a rain-soaked field in Bloomington, Indiana. The conditions led to the game’s start being delayed twice, from a scheduled 6 p.m. kickoff to an eventual 8:15 p.m. start. While the rain subsided before kickoff, its remnants were apparent as the teams vied for early possession. Passes from both sides fizzed along the surface, and several players struggled for footing — including Maryland winger Dominic Ayella, who slipped and fell while attempting to latch onto a chance five minutes in. Rodrigo Neri had the first clear chance of the game in the 12th minute, stealing an errant backpass, but he fired a tame shot from the edge of the box. After Maryland controlled the opening 15 minutes, Indiana grew into the game, earning the best opportunity of the first half midway through the period. A turnover deep in Maryland’s half let former Terp Stephane Njike slide a pass to a wide-open Bogard inside the box. The striker let the ball roll across his body and onto his left foot, but with goalkeeper Laurin Mack and a defender closing down, Bogard blazed his shot into the black sky. Head coach Sasho Cirovski brought on counterattacking threats in striker Said El Eyssami and winger Marco Wright soon thereafter to try to give Maryland another dimension offensively, but the Terps still couldn’t find a second shot on goal before halftime. In the 36th minute, Bogard and Njike each had a chance to test Mack, but the freshmen center back tandem of Sekyi and Franklin Affanyi each blocked a shot to keep the game scoreless. Sekyi’s night nearly went from bad to worse in the 55th minute, when he lunged into the back of Indiana midfielder Charlie Heuer while attempting to catch up on a breakaway. Referees didn’t award a penalty on the field and upheld the decision after a review that lasted several minutes. The veteran lefty struck out 200 hitters and only walked 31, trailing only Jacob Misiorowski in strikeout-to-walk ratio. Sale also closed out Game 3 of the National League Wild Card Round in heroic fashion at Truist Park as the Braves advanced past the Phillies to move on to the NLDS. In three seasons with the Braves, Sale has been named to the All-MLB First Team twice. item.title: Rutgers women's basketball wins but major scare from Monmouth, Gigi Gamble
item.description: PISCATAWAY -- The Rutgers women's basketball team avoided an upset Wednesday night when the Scarlet Knights came back from 17-point deficit to defeat Monmouth University 64-62. With the game tied 62-62, Mia Pauldo got the ball off the screen, drove right, stopped and hit a midrange jumper to give Rutgers the lead with 3.4 seconds left. The possession before, Pauldo hit a floater in the paint to get the lead before Monmouth's Gigi Gamble tied it up with free throws. More: Rutgers women's basketball has Hope. Masonius comes home for new beginning | Exclusive Monmouth led by as much as 17 points but the game was tied after Rutgers went on an 18-6 run in the third quarter. "Honestly, we had this game," said Monmouth's Gigi Gamble, who had a game-high 30 was named the Coastal Athletic Conference Preseason Player of the Year. "We had it, it hurts, but it should give us more fuel, more fight, more hunger, more heart." "We're going to keep building off it. So I'm not worried about this loss." Rutgers is 4-0 but this was by far the closest call the Big Ten team has had. "Coach (Gary Redus) had a talk while I was on the bench and he said the best players aren't who they are when things are only going good for them, they're who they are when things are going bad for them," said Pauldo, who scored 7 points in the first half but finished with a team-high 17. "I took that in and was like, yeah I want to be the best player and I was messing up in the first half and I wasn't focused enough. And I was like to take responsibility in this game, if we really want to win this game I got to lock in and step up and be the best player." Monmouth got a chance to tie with 3.0 seconds left but turned the ball over on the inbounds to seal the win for the Scarlet Knights. The Scarlet Knights (4-0) came out the gate slow but picked up the defensive pressure in the second half to hold off a Monmouth (2-1) team that's projected to win the Coastal Athletic Association Conference. So far this season, Rutgers has faced mid-majors and Tuesday was no different, but the level of pressure was different. Redus labeled the game a "wake up call." "I would've liked us to be a little bit more aggressive tonight," Redus said. "I felt like we could've come out and we could've had more aggression especially on the defensive end. I didn't like our defensive effort at all in the first half. That was the issue. We had nine points in the first quarter but the offense is gonna be hit or miss at times with any team. Especially in close games, it's your defense that has to carry you." They shot 55% in the first half so that's what I told them, it was the defense." One of the biggest bright spots for Rutgers was the way it was able share the ball. Eight different Scarlet Knights were able to score the ball on Wednesday which came in handy. Especially in the third quarter when Rutgers went on a 18-2 run to go into the last quarter tied 44-44. Rutgers first lead came with 9:28 left in the last quarter

item.title: Rangers fend off Flames 3-1 to win final visit to Saddledome
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Rangers bade farewell to Scotiabank Saddledome by continuing their solid play on a four-game swing through the Pacific Northwest with a 3-1 victory over the Calgary Flames on Wednesday night. Mika Zibanejad scored twice in the second period, Tye Kartye put the game away with an empty-netter and Joonas Korpisalo made 30 saves for his second victory in as many games with the Rangers after returning from a foot injury . Alexis Lafreniere assisted on both of Zibanejad’s goals as the Rangers won for just the 10th time (10-21-2 with four ties) in their 37 visits to the Saddledome since it opened in 1983. The Flames will move into the new Scotia Place next season. New York (11-8-1) improved to 11-1-0 when scoring first. The Rangers are 2-1-0 heading into the final game of their trips against the NHL’s worst team, the Vancouver Canucks (3-16-1), on Friday. Alan Klapka scored a third-period power-play goal and Devin Cooley made 21 saves for the Flames (8-10-1). Calgary had won six of its seven previous games against the Rangers at the Saddledome. Mika Zibanejad’s two goals carry Rangers past Flames 3-1 in Saddledome finale The Rangers found themselves killing a penalty right away when Gabe Perreault was called for hooking Calgary’s Jacob Middleton at 1:13. But the NHL’s best penalty kill had little trouble keeping the Flames off the board. Korpisalo came up big shortly before the four-minute mark when he went left to right and denied Zane Parekh’s wraparound attempt with his catching glove. The Flames had a 6-2 advantage in shots in the first eight minutes, but the Rangers began to control more of the play after that, forcing Cooley to be sharp. However, the Flames forced Korpisalo to be sharp again late in the period; he denied Matvei Gridin from close-in with just over a minute remaining. The period ended 0-0, with the Flames outshooting the Rangers 9-8 — but with New York having the edge in attempts (21-16) and hits (14-8). WHAT A SAVE, KORPI 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/XUh99QADqS — New York Rangers (@NYRangers) November 12, 2026 The Rangers broke the scoreless tie 59 seconds into the second period on the first of Zibanejad’s two goals, Lafreniere’s breakout pass sent him racing through center ice and then into the right circle, where he shoveled a feed to the front of the net. The pass didn’t find a teammate — but it did wind up in the back of the net after hitting Cooley, giving New York a 1-0 lead. “I tried to bank it off him,” Zibanejad said postgame. “I saw him leave the post.” The Rangers continued to dominate play through the first half of the period and doubled their lead at 10:52 on a power-play rocket by Zibanejad from the lower left circle. No. 93 won the face-off after ex-Ranger Ryan Strome was sent off for holding Kartye at 10:39 and drifted over to his favorite spot, where Pavel Dorofeyev fed him a perfect cross-ice pass for a one-timer that Cooley had no chance to stop. item.title: Ford Veterans Day Classic at Daytona is a hit. Will it return? If so, where?
item.description: Yes, we can call it the “inaugural” Veterans Day Classic at Daytona. We’ll eventually see the TV numbers from USA Network’s Wednesday night coverage. But the eyeball test suggests a hit for the Ford Motor Company, its Ford Racing division, and the combo of NASCAR and Daytona International Speedway. “We love throwing races. We love throwing big events. We love partnering with friends like Ford,” Speedway President Frank Kelleher said Wednesday night while mixing in the thick FanZone crowd. Logistics can be, you know, logistical, and sometimes timing and schedules are a challenge, but Veterans Day appears to fall in a unique place on the calendar — right after the NASCAR season, just before the holidays start dominating the scene. Thankfully, Veterans Day isn’t going anywhere, and my guess is Ford will always have cars to sell, so maybe this becomes a yearly thing. “I would love it,” Kelleher said. “We know how to execute high-level music acts. Music and racing are definitely in our DNA.” Except he then tossed in a wrinkle worth noting. “We will be excited to chat with Ford and everyone involved in the weeks to come and see if it makes sense to bring it back, whether it be here at Daytona International Speedway or perhaps at another speedway.” Will Veterans Day Classic return? Probably. But where? … Or perhaps at another Speedway. That seems like a logical move. However, and back to logistics, Wednesday’s event had the advantage of blending into an existing Daytona race week — Historic Sportscar Racing’s 12th annual Daytona Classic 24, which started Wednesday and runs through Sunday. The track’s race operations were already in place, which brings a nice advantage. We’re LIVE from Daytona for the Veterans Day Classic! 🇺🇸🏁 📺 : USA Netwok pic.twitter.com/cZOeXCYmIm — NASCAR on USA (@NASCARonUSA) November 12, 2026 Given the HSR presence, the garage area was wall-to-wall with a wide variety of yesterday’s racing machinery, including cars that previously ran here in both stock-car and sportscar races. For anyone who walked the grounds and saw the recent racing equipment and virtual museum pieces, there was contrast, since one of two threads running through it all was promotion of Ford’s new Mustang Dark Horse. The NASCAR version of the new Mustang was unveiled Wednesday afternoon at the museum outside Turn 4. The road-racing version was center stage for the 30-minute race on Daytona’s Rolex 24 road course. The other thread, of course, was Veterans Day. The Speedway and NASCAR have always leaned heavily toward the promotion of our nation’s military and its veterans. Usually, it’s part of the show. Wednesday, that theme blanketed the entire evening of loud music and louder machines. And you’d have a hard time finding anything other than a thumbs-up from those who joined the festivities. Bob Turley was the first Yankee to be named a Cy Young winner in 1958, while Whitey Ford and Sparky Lyle won theirs in 1961 and 1977, respectively. Before Schlittler, the last Yankees hurler to win the Cy Young was Gerrit Cole in 2023. The 25-year-old Schlittler won the award in just his second season in the big leagues. item.title: Revived Fuellkrug relishes home comforts on Germany return
item.description: Niclas Fuellkrug (R) has been in top form since returning to Werder Bremen (Kirill KUDRYAVTSEV) After ill-fated stints at West Ham and AC Milan, striker Niclas Fuellkrug's rich vein of form since his Werder Bremen return has been capped with a Germany recall. Germany coach Jurgen Klopp brought Fuellkrug back into the fold for Nations League fixtures against Serbia on Friday and the Netherlands next week. Fuellkrug has not played an international game since a Nations League third-place playoff loss to France in June 2025. While Klopp, who has a contract until after the 2030 World Cup, has stated his focus is on youth and building for the future, Fuellkrug made himself impossible to ignore. Currently the Bundesliga's top scorer ahead of Harry Kane, the 33-year-old has 12 goals in 11 matches in all competitions, having managed only four in two seasons after leaving Germany for West Ham. Klopp admitted "sometimes form trumps everything else". "He made his case with a wide variety of goals... and almost all of them were spectacular," said Klopp. Fuellkrug also has an excellent record for Germany with 14 goals in just 24 appearances, many of which came as a substitute. Fuellkrug has a simple explanation for his form since returning to Bremen on a season-long loan from now-Championship side West Ham. "It's my footballing home," Fuellkrug said of the club he first joined aged 14. "Everyone sleeps better in their own bed. I just feel completely at ease here." Fuellkrug became the latest striker to endure an unhappy time at West Ham, a club which has become a graveyard for promising European forwards. He scored just three times in an injury-hit 18 months in London. But while he may not have gotten among the goals, his endeared himself to some of the fanbase with his typically German honesty. After conceding late to draw 1-1 at home to Southampton in April 2025, Fuellkrug spoke his mind, using a swear word to describe the Hammers' performance, with the West Ham fans then using his quote to create a chant referencing him. Fuellkrug's honesty has also won him support among many in Germany, where the gap-toothed journeyman is seen as an antidote to the modern image-conscious footballer. "I couldn't stay fit," Fuellkrug said of his struggles abroad, adding: "The key is staying fit and having a team around me that looks for me -- and passes me the ball when the moment is right. "That's the key -- I think I've been able to prove that now." - Klose an 'inspiration' - Fuellkrug is in blistering form but his call-up highlights how bare the cupboard now is in a country once known for producing top-class forwards. The four-time world champions have produced strikers like Gerd Mueller, Fritz Walter, Ulf Kirsten, Rudi Voeller and Jurgen Klinsmann. But Germany have not had a top-class number nine since 2014 World Cup-winner Miroslav Klose. Of Germany's current generation, Kai Havertz regularly starts up front but the Arsenal man has never been an out-and-out goalscorer.

item.title: Deshaun Watson makes feelings clear on Texans reunion as DeMeco Ryans delivers verdict
item.description: Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images Deshaun Watson has played down the significance of facing his former team as the Cleveland Browns prepare to take on the Houston Texans in Week 10. The quarterback will meet Houston for just the second time since being traded to Cleveland, having previously spent the first four seasons of his NFL career with the franchise that drafted him 12th overall in 2017. However, Watson insists his attention is firmly on helping the Browns return to winning ways and remain in the playoff hunt. DeMeco Ryans praises Deshaun Watson ahead of Houston Texans reunion Speaking to reporters, Watson made it clear that the personal storyline surrounding the reunion was no longer important to him. “It’s a big opportunity for us. Get back on the winning track, especially get in front of our home fans. That’s the ultimate focus, is focus on that. All the outside things, going against my former team, that stuff was in the past. Four, five years ago? Yeah, it was a big deal,” Watson said. “Now, I think both sides have moved on, and we’re just both trying to find ways to win and continue to put ourselves in position for later on down the road.” Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans also had plenty of praise for Watson, highlighting his decision-making and ability to escape pressure. “I’ve seen a guy who’s being very decisive with the football. He’s getting the ball out of his hands very quickly. When it’s not there, it’s his athletic ability to escape the pocket,” Ryans said. He also pointed to Watson’s performances in important moments, adding: “The thing that showed up the most for me watching the Browns throughout this year is how they performed in those clutch moments and those two-minute moments situations. Deshaun has really rose to the occasion, and he’s made some really big plays to put their team in position to win a lot of football games.” Houston defensive end Will Anderson Jr. expects the quarterback’s mobility to present a difficult challenge. Anderson described Watson as a dynamic quarterback and stressed that the Texans’ defensive line must rush together rather than leave gaps for him to exploit. Meanwhile, C.J. Stroud was equally respectful of his fellow quarterback, saying: “I got a lot of appreciation for Deshaun. He was good to me when I was in college, and been a big fan of his when he played here as well.” The Browns enter the matchup at 5-3, while Watson will be looking to help his side get back on track against a Houston team that knows his game well.
